text:
ConocoPhillips fell 0.98% today to $135.86, giving back some of the sharp gains from the past two days despite oil prices holding relatively steady. The stock had surged nearly $4 on Tuesday and Wednesday as U.S. oil climbed above $91 a barrel on escalating Iran-Kuwait tensions and direct military strikes between Washington and Tehran. Today's pullback came even as geopolitical risk remained elevated—suggesting investors may be taking profits after the week's 9% oil rally, or reassessing the durability of those gains after Trump indicated the conflict won't last long.

The oil market itself has been volatile but supportive: U.S. crude at $91.48 and global Brent at $96.02 are still meaningfully higher than where the week started, which should help an integrated producer like ConocoPhillips. The pause in upward momentum today likely reflects uncertainty about whether Middle East tensions will sustain oil's recent strength or fade quickly as the Trump administration suggests.
